questions.question: Which direct observation did the authors identify as evidence for a π-hole, and which molecule served as the no-π-hole comparison?

options.A: KPFM resolved a central electrostatic feature in FCl-An, absent in anthracene (An)
options.B: STM resolved a central depression in An, absent in FCl-An
options.C: nc-AFM resolved a central bond in both molecules, but DFT assigned it only to An
options.D: XPS detected a positive central charge in An, but not in FCl-An

questions.rationale: The work reports direct KPFM visualization in halogenated FCl-An and its absence in unsubstituted anthracene.
questions.evidence_quote: we experimentally confirm the existence of the π-hole in 9,10-Dichlorooctafluoroanthracene C14F8Cl2 (FCl-An) molecule and, at the same time, its absence in anthracene C14H10 (An).

questions.question: What composition and geometry characterize the experimentally observed mixed molecular self-assembly on Au(111)?

options.A: A square cell with two An and one FCl-An
options.B: A rhombic periodic cell with one An and two FCl-An
options.C: A hexagonal cell with equal numbers of An and FCl-An
options.D: A rectangular cell with one An and three FCl-An

questions.rationale: The combined high-resolution nc-AFM and DFT assignment identifies a rhombus containing one anthracene and two FCl-An molecules.
questions.evidence_quote: The supramolecular assembly comprises a rhombic periodic structure with one An and two FCl-An molecules in the unit cell

questions.question: Which intermolecular interactions did the authors invoke to explain the organization of the mixed assembly?

options.A: Attraction between F− atoms, chlorine σ-holes and positively charged hydrogens
options.B: Repulsion between F− atoms and attraction between chlorine σ-holes only
options.C: Metal coordination between chlorine and Au atoms, with hydrogen bonding between An molecules
options.D: Dispersion between the carbon skeletons without an electrostatic contribution

questions.rationale: The paper assigns the arrangement to electrostatic attractions among negatively charged fluorines, chlorine σ-holes, and positively charged hydrogens.
questions.evidence_quote: The arrangement is dictated by attractive intermolecular electrostatic interactions between negatively charged fluorine atoms, sigmahole on chlorine, and positively charged hydrogen atoms

questions.question: Why did the authors regard the nc-AFM images alone as insufficient evidence of the π-hole?

options.A: The carbon-skeleton contrast was similar, while FCl-An appeared brighter from a topographic effect
options.B: The CO tip chemically transformed the molecules during scanning
options.C: The images had no atomic resolution at the 4.8 K measurement temperature
options.D: The π-hole appeared only after KPFM bias compensation, not in any molecular image

questions.rationale: They explicitly note comparable skeleton contrast and an apparent brightness difference due to topography, so they turned to KPFM for charge mapping.
questions.evidence_quote: AFM images apparently do not provide any direct experimental evidence of π-hole.

questions.question: What determines the KPFM local-contact-potential contrast at sufficiently short tip–sample separation in this experiment?

options.A: Short-range electrostatic interaction between the tip apex and surface, enabling charge-distribution mapping
options.B: Long-range van der Waals attraction alone, independent of molecular charge
options.C: The topographic height difference, which directly equals the LCPD signal
options.D: The Pauli repulsion at the CO tip, which replaces electrostatic contrast

questions.rationale: The authors explain that at short range LCPD is affected by a short-range electrostatic interaction, permitting atomic-resolution charge mapping.
questions.evidence_quote: At short tip-sample distances, the magnitude of the LCPD is affected by a short-range electrostatic interaction acting between the tip apex and surfaces, which enables us to map the charge distribution

questions.question: Why did the authors avoid the very shortest tip–sample distances for KPFM acquisition?

options.A: Tip relaxation can distort the LCPD parabola and create artifacts, so a height near Δf minima was chosen
options.B: The π-hole is screened at close range, so the tip was moved far enough to remove all intramolecular contrast
options.C: The Au surface becomes chemically reactive below the Δf minima
options.D: The CO tip loses functionalization when the LCPD signal becomes parabolic

questions.rationale: At short distances relaxations can cause deviations from parabolic LCPD behavior, unlike their beneficial role in nc-AFM imaging.
questions.evidence_quote: in KPFM measurement, such relaxations cause a noticeable deviation in the LCPD signal from its parabolic shape

questions.question: How did the observed KPFM contrast change as the tip approached the surface?

options.A: Far tips showed no intramolecular features, while reducing the separation made submolecular contrast more pronounced
options.B: Far tips resolved the π-hole best, while closer approach removed all charge contrast
options.C: The contrast was independent of distance until the CO tip touched the molecular plane
options.D: Closer approach increased only topographic contrast and never produced submolecular features

questions.rationale: The paper states that intramolecular detail is absent at far separation and emerges increasingly as the tip approaches.
questions.evidence_quote: when the tipsample distance is far, the KPFM images do not exhibit intramolecular features. As the tipsample distance decreases, submolecular contrast becomes increasingly pronounced.

questions.question: How did the measured adsorption heights compare for An and FCl-An on Au(111)?

options.A: An was 330 pm and FCl-An 360 pm above Au(111), a 30 pm difference
options.B: An was 360 pm and FCl-An 330 pm, a 30 pm difference
options.C: Both were 330 pm, despite a 30 pm difference in Δf minima
options.D: An was 325 pm and FCl-An 360 pm, matching identical DFT heights

questions.rationale: Force-distance spectroscopy gave relative adsorption heights of 330 and 360 pm, respectively, with the chlorinated molecule higher.
questions.evidence_quote: the relative height of the molecules above the Au(111) surface, to be 330 and 360 pm for An and FCl-An, respectively.

questions.question: What electronic effect of the π-hole was proposed to explain FCl-An's greater adsorption height?

options.A: It increases ionization potential, suppressing interfacial charge induction and weakening induced electrostatic attraction
options.B: It lowers ionization potential, increasing charge transfer and strengthening substrate binding
options.C: It creates strong orbital hybridization that pushes the molecule farther from the surface
options.D: It removes dispersion attraction and makes adsorption purely repulsive

questions.rationale: The paper attributes reduced induced density and larger adsorption height to the π-hole's increase of ionization potential.
questions.evidence_quote: the presence of π-hole increases the ionization potential and consequently suppresses the charge density induction at the molecule/metal interface.

questions.question: Which acquisition and fitting procedure was used to construct the LCPD maps?

options.A: Fit parabolas to Δf(V,x,y) spectra collected over a 64×80 grid spanning 3×5 nm², then map the parabola maxima
options.B: Map constant-current STM at 64×80 points and infer LCPD from the current minimum
options.C: Fit Gaussian curves to 600 KPFM spectra acquired on a 3×5 pixel grid
options.D: Average Δf at fixed ±150 mV over a 64×80 grid and label the mean as LCPD

questions.rationale: The methods specify a parabolic fit at each position on a 64-by-80 rectangular grid of 3-by-5 nm dimensions; the maximum gives LCPD.
questions.evidence_quote: LCPD maps were obtained by fitting a parabolic expression to frequency shift vs bias spectroscopies (Δf(V, x, y)) collected at all the points of a 64 x 80 pixels rectangular grid of size 3 nm x 5 nm.
